name: Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS)
description: A large multilingual corpus suitable for speech research, derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox. The dataset consists of 8 languages, including about 44.5K hours of English and a total of about 6K hours for other languages (German, Dutch, Spanish, French, Portuguese, Italian, Polish).
creator: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert (Facebook AI Research)
inLanguage: en, de, nl, es, fr, pt, it, pl
citeAs: Vineel Pratap, Qiantong Xu, Anuroop Sriram, Gabriel Synnaeve, Ronan Collobert. MLS: A Large-Scale Multilingual Dataset for Speech Research. arXiv:2012.03411v2 [eess.AS], December 22, 2020.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset is derived from read audiobooks from LibriVox. Audio files were downloaded using LibriLight open source library tools. All audio data was downsampled from 48kHz to 16kHz. Long audio files were segmented into 10-20 second segments using trained acoustic models with Time-Depth Separable (TDS) Convolutions and Auto-Segmentation Criterion (ASG) loss. Segmentation was performed by running inference on audio to generate viterbi token sequences with timestamps, then splitting at silence intervals between 10-20 seconds.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: LibriVox audiobooks, which are based on Project Gutenberg text data. For English, 60K hours of audiobooks were read from four major website domains: gutenberg.org, archive.org, ccel.org, and hathitrust.org. For other languages, text sources were extracted from various domains using automated parsers and manual approaches.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Numbers in the text were replaced with corresponding aligned words from pseudo labels. Heuristics were applied to handle hyphens and apostrophes: rare words with hyphens or apostrophes were replaced based on alignment with pseudo labels. End-of-line hyphenation was removed and word parts were joined into single words.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Text normalization was performed using NFKC normalization. Unwanted characters like punctuations, subscript/superscripts, emojis, and escape symbols were removed. Valid unicode characters were filtered based on language orthography. Books with corrupted metadata, missing title or speaker information were removed. Audios with multiple speakers (e.g., 'Dramatic Reading') were removed. Only the latest version of books sharing the same authors and title were kept. Candidate transcripts were filtered if WER between candidate transcript and pseudo label was >40%. Books with title edit distance less than 2 from dev/test books were removed. Books with more than 1% of 5-grams appearing in dev/test sets were removed.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Human evaluation was performed on development and test sets. Human transcribers listened to audio files while viewing transcripts and were asked to correct only 'clear and obvious' errors to ensure high quality without introducing bias.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: WER between generated transcripts and human-rated transcripts was measured. Error rates ranged from 1.93% (Spanish dev) to 12.64% (Portuguese dev).
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Trained acoustic models using Time-Depth Separable (TDS) Convolutions with Auto-Segmentation Criterion (ASG) loss were used to generate pseudo labels. For English, a pre-trained model using TDS encoder and CTC loss on LibriSpeech was used. Beam-search decoding with 4-gram language models was performed. A gender classifier (SVM with RBF kernel trained on LibriSpeech) was used to label speaker gender with 95% test accuracy.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Gender (speakers were labeled by gender using a classifier and balanced in development and test sets)
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is read-speech only, derived from audiobooks. For Polish, the high OOV rate (13.39%) negatively impacts WER when performing LM decoding with constrained lexicon. The MLS development and test sets for English were chosen to be harder than LibriSpeech dev-/test-other partitions (speakers with WER higher than 80% of dev-other sets were selected). Text sources for some audiobooks could not be downloaded due to invalid links or domain diversity, requiring manual approaches. The pseudo label generation process may not always have correct transcriptions, affecting the number replacement procedure.
rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is suitable for Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) research and Text-To-Speech (TTS) research. It can be used for training, validation, and testing ASR models. Limited supervision datasets (10 hour, 1 hour, and six 10-minute sets) are provided for low resource training benchmarks. The dataset can extend LibriTTS for multilingual TTS research.
